kf: Melanoma outcome depends mostly on **Breslow thickness**, **ulceration** and nodal status (AJCC 8th edition).
Excision biopsy with a 2 mm margin first; then **wide local excision** (1 cm for <1 mm; 1–2 cm for 1–2 mm; 2 cm for >2 mm thickness).
Sentinel lymph node biopsy offered from stage IB (pT1b) upwards (NICE NG14).
Adjuvant immunotherapy or BRAF/MEK inhibitors for resected stage III (and some IIB/C); systemic therapy for stage IV.
Follow-up by stage; teach self-examination of skin and lymph nodes.
myths: **"Removing the mole means it's all gone"**: thicker melanomas need wide excision and staging.
patho_lead: The deeper a melanoma grows, the more likely it has **reached lymphatics and blood vessels**.

mech.t: Early melanoma spreads within the epidermis: excellent prognosis.
Invasion into the dermis gives access to lymphatics and vessels.
mech.cap: Breslow thickness: measured from the granular layer to the deepest tumour cell.

mech.t: Ulceration and high mitotic rate mark aggressive biology.
Wide local excision removes in-transit cells around the scar.
mech.cap: Wide local excision margins by Breslow thickness.

comp: Local recurrence, in-transit and nodal metastases, distant spread (lung, liver, brain).
prog: Five-year survival over 95% for thin melanoma (<1 mm); much lower with nodal or distant disease.
